questions.question: Pipe A is capable of filling a tank in 16 minutes while Pipe B can fill the same tank in 24 minutes. Both pipes are opened together, but after 4 minutes, the rate of Pipe A doubles and the rate of Pipe B becomes half of its original. How many more minutes will it take to fill the tank completely?
questions.questionHtml: Pipe A is capable of filling a tank in 16 minutes while Pipe B can fill the same tank in 24 minutes. Both pipes are opened together, but after 4 minutes, the rate of Pipe A doubles and the rate of Pipe B becomes half of its original. How many more minutes will it take to fill the tank completely?
questions.solution:
⇒ Total Work = LCM(16, 24) = 48 units

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe A = 48 ÷ 16 = 3 units/min, Efficiency of Pipe B = 48 ÷ 24 = 2 units/min

⇒ Combined efficiency for first 4 minutes = 3 + 2 = 5 units/min, Work done in first 4 minutes = 5 × 4 = 20 units

⇒ Remaining work = 48 − 20 = 28 units

⇒ New rate of Pipe A = 2 × 3 = 6 units/min, New rate of Pipe B = 2 ÷ 2 = 1 unit/min

⇒ New combined efficiency = 6 + 1 = 7 units/min, Time to fill remaining work = 28 ÷ 7 = 4 minutes

questions.question: A circle is inscribed within a right triangle. Considering that the lengths of the two legs measure 6 cm and 8 cm, what is the radius of the inscribed circle?
questions.questionHtml: A circle is inscribed within a right triangle. Considering that the lengths of the two legs measure 6 cm and 8 cm, what is the radius of the inscribed circle?
questions.solution:
Hypotenuse (c) = √(62 + 82) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 cm

Semi-perimeter = (6 + 8 + 10) ÷ 2 = 12 cm

Area = (1 ÷ 2) × 6 × 8 = 24 cm2

Radius (r) = Area ÷ Semi-perimeter = 24 ÷ 12 = 2 cm

Sentence 2 introduces Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) and its foundational concept of "objects." Sentence 1 explains the "class" as a critical blueprint concept in OOP. Sentence 3 elaborates on how this concept allows programmers to define structure and behavior. Sentence 4 highlights the main advantage of OOP, tying it back to its practical utility.  

The chronology follows logically because Sentence 2 establishes the main topic, Sentence 1 provides a key detail, Sentence 3 describes its practical application, and Sentence 4 concludes with the benefit. This structure ensures a coherent flow from introduction to conclusion.
